Simplified text: Definitions in Aadhaar Act, 2016
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) "Aadhaar number" means an identification number issued to an individual under section 3(3), including any alternative virtual identity generated under section 3(4).
(aa) "Aadhaar ecosystem" includes enrolling agencies, Registrars, requesting entities, offline verification-seeking entities, and any other specified entities.
(b) "Aadhaar number holder" means an individual who has been issued an Aadhaar number under this Act.
(ba) "Adjudicating Officer" means an officer appointed under section 33B.
(bb) "Appellate Tribunal" means the tribunal referred to in section 33C.
(c) "authentication" means the process of submitting an individual's Aadhaar number along with demographic or biometric information for verification by the Central Identities Data Repository.
(d) "authentication record" means the record of the time of authentication, the identity of the requesting entity, and the response provided by the Authority.
(e) "Authority" means the Unique Identification Authority of India established under section 11.
(f) "benefit" means any advantage, gift, reward, relief, or payment provided to an individual or group of individuals, as notified by the Central Government.
(g) "biometric information" means photograph, fingerprint, iris scan, or other specified biological attributes.
(h) "Central Identities Data Repository" means a centralized database containing all Aadhaar numbers issued, demographic and biometric information, and related data.
(i) "Chairperson" means the Chairperson of the Authority appointed under section 12.
(ia) "child" means a person under eighteen years of age.
(j) "core biometric information" means fingerprint, iris scan, or other specified biological attributes.
(k) "demographic information" includes information related to name, date of birth, address, and other relevant details, as specified by regulations.
(l) "enrolling agency" means an agency appointed for collecting demographic and biometric information under this Act.
(m) "enrolment" means the process to collect demographic and biometric information from individuals for issuing Aadhaar numbers.
(n) "identity information" includes Aadhaar number, biometric information, and demographic information.
(o) "Member" includes the Chairperson and Members of the Authority.
(p) "notification" means a notification published in the Official Gazette.
(pa) "offline verification" means the process of verifying the identity of an Aadhaar number holder without authentication, through specified offline modes.
(pb) "offline verification-seeking entity" means any entity desiring offline verification of an Aadhaar number holder.
(q) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
(r) "records of entitlement" means records of benefits, subsidies, or services provided to or availed by any individual under any program.
(s) "Registrar" means any entity authorized for enrolling individuals under this Act.
(t) "regulations" means the regulations made by the Authority under this Act.
(u) "requesting entity" means an agency or person submitting Aadhaar number, demographic information, or biometric information for authentication.
(v) "resident" means an individual who has resided in India for a specified period preceding the date of enrollment.
(w) "service" means any provision, facility, utility, or assistance provided to an individual or group of individuals, as notified by the Central Government.
(x) "subsidy" means any form of aid, support, grant, or appropriation in cash or kind provided to an individual or group of individuals, as notified by the Central Government.
(Note: Some sections and dates have been mentioned in regards to amendments made to the Act.)

SECTION 3 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
Chapter II
Enrolment
3. Aadhaar number.-
(1) Every resident shall be entitled to obtain an Aadhaar number by submitting his demographic information and biometric information by undergoing the process of enrolment:
Provided that the Central Government may, from time to time, notify such other category of individuals who may be entitled to obtain an Aadhaar number.
(2) The enrolling agency shall, at the time of enrolment, inform the individual undergoing enrolment of the following details in such manner as may be specified by regulations, namely:-
(a) the manner in which the information shall be used;
(b) the nature of recipients with whom the information is intended to be shared during authentication; and
(c) the existence of a right to access information, the procedure for making requests for such access, and details of the person or department in-charge to whom such requests can be made.
(3) On receipt of the demographic information and biometric information under sub-section (1), the Authority shall, after verifying the information, in such manner as may be specified by regulations, issue an Aadhaar number to such individual.
1[(4) The Aadhaar number issued to an individual under sub-section (3) shall be a twelve-digit identification number and any alternative virtual identity as an alternative to the actual Aadhaar number of an individual that shall be generated by the Authority in such manner as may be specified by regulations.]
1. Ins. by Act 14 of 2019, s. 4 (w.e.f. 25-7-2019).

simplified_text:
Entitlement to Aadhaar Number:
Every resident has the right to get an Aadhaar number by providing their demographic and biometric information during the enrollment process. The Central Government may also identify other groups of individuals who are entitled to obtain an Aadhaar number.


Details Provided During Enrollment:
The enrolling agency must inform the individual being enrolled about the following details:
- How the information will be used
- The recipients with whom the information will be shared for authentication
- The right to access the information, the process for making access requests, and the contact details for the person or department in charge of handling such requests.


Aadhaar Number Issuance:
Upon receiving the demographic and biometric information, the Authority will verify the information and issue a twelve-digit Aadhaar number to the individual. Additionally, an alternative virtual identity may be generated as specified by regulations.

SECTION 4 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
4. Properties of Aadhaar number.-
(1) An Aadhaar number, issued to an individual shall not be re-assigned to any other individual.
(2) An Aadhaar number shall be a random number and bear no relation to the attributes or identity of the Aadhaar number holder.
1[(3) Every Aadhaar number holder to establish his identity, may voluntarily use his Aadhaar number in physical or electronic form by way of authentication or offline verification, or in such other form as may be notified, in such manner as may be specified by regulations.
Explanation.- For the purposes of this section, voluntary use of the Aadhaar number by way of authentication means the use of such Aadhaar number only with the informed consent of the Aadhaar number holder.
(4) An entity may be allowed to perform authentication, if the Authority is satisfied that the requesting entity is-
(a) compliant with such standards of privacy and security as may be specified by regulations; and
(b) (i) permitted to offer authentication services under the provisions of any other law made by Parliament; or
(ii) seeking authentication for such purpose, as the Central Government in consultation with the Authority, and in the interest of State, may prescribe.
(5) The Authority may, by regulations, decide whether a requesting entity shall be permitted the use of the actual Aadhaar number during authentication or only an alternative virtual identity.
(6) Every requesting entity to whom an authentication request is made by an Aadhaar number holder under sub-section (3) shall inform to the Aadhaar number holder of alternate and viable means of identification and shall not deny any service to him for refusing to, or being unable to, undergo authentication.
(7) Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing provisions, mandatory authentication of an Aadhaar number holder for the provision of any service shall take place if such authentication is required by a law made by Parliament.]
1. Subs. by Act 14 of 2019, s. 6, for Sub-section (3) (w.e.f. 25-7-2019).
simplified_text:
Simplified text: Properties of Aadhaar Number:
1. The Aadhaar number assigned to an individual cannot be given to another person.
2. The Aadhaar number is a random number and does not reveal any specific information about the person it is assigned to.
3. An individual can use their Aadhaar number, with their consent, to prove their identity in physical or electronic form. They can also use other authorized methods notified by regulations.
4. An organization can perform authentication if it meets privacy and security standards specified by regulations and is permitted to offer authentication services under the law. The Central Government, in consultation with the Authority, may prescribe the purpose for seeking authentication.
5. The Authority can decide whether an organization can use the actual Aadhaar number or an alternative virtual identity during authentication.
6. If an Aadhaar number holder chooses not to undergo authentication, the requesting organization must provide alternate means of identification and cannot deny service.
7. Mandatory authentication of an Aadhaar number holder for any service will only occur if required by a law passed by Parliament.

SECTION 7 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
Chapter III
Authentication
7. Proof of Aadhaar number necessary for receipt of certain subsidies, benefits and services, etc.-
The Central Government or, as the case may be, the State Government may, for the purpose of establishing identity of an individual as a condition for receipt of a subsidy, benefit or service for which the expenditure is incurred from, or the receipt therefrom forms part of, the Consolidated Fund of India, 1[or the Consolidated Fund of State] require that such individual undergo authentication, or furnish proof of possession of Aadhaar number or in the case of an individual to whom no Aadhaar number has been assigned, such individual makes an application for enrolment:
Provided that if an Aadhaar number is not assigned to an individual, the individual shall be offered alternate and viable means of identification for delivery of the subsidy, benefit or service.
1. Ins. by Act 14 of 2019, s. 7 (w.e.f. 25-7-2019).

Simplified text: 
Proving Identity for Government Benefits:
The Central or State Government can require individuals to prove their identity to receive certain subsidies, benefits, or services, if the funds come from the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of a State. This can be done through authenticating their identity using Aadhaar or providing proof of possessing an Aadhaar number. If an individual does not have an Aadhaar number, they can apply to enroll for it. If an Aadhaar number is not assigned to an individual, the government must offer them alternative means of identification to receive the subsidy, benefit, or service.

SECTION 8 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
8. Authentication of Aadhaar number.-
(1) The Authority shall perform authentication of the Aadhaar number of an Aadhaar number holder submitted by any requesting entity, in relation to his biometric information or demographic information, subject to such conditions and on payment of such fees and in such manner as may be specified by regulations.
(2) A requesting entity shall-
(a) unless otherwise provided in this Act, obtain the consent of an individual 2[or in the case of a child obtain the consent of his parent or guardian] before collecting his identity information for the purposes of authentication in such manner as may be specified by regulations; and
(b) ensure that the identity information of an individual is only used for submission to the Central Identities Data Repository for authentication.
2[Provided that the requesting entity shall, in case of failure to authenticate due to illness, injury or infirmity owing to old age or otherwise or any technical or other reasons, provide such alternate and viable means of identification of the individual, as may be specified by regulations.]
(3) A requesting entity shall inform, in such manner as may be specified by regulations, the individual submitting his identity information for authentication 2[or in the case of a child, his parent or guardian], the following details with respect to authentication, namely:-
(a) the nature of information that may be shared upon authentication;
(b) the uses to which the information received during authentication may be put by the requesting entity; and
(c) alternatives to submission of identity information to the requesting entity.
(4) The Authority shall respond to an authentication query with a positive, negative or any other appropriate response sharing such identity information excluding any core biometric information.
2. Ins. by s. 8, ibid, (w.e.f. 25-7-2019).

Simplified text: 
Using Aadhaar Number for Verification:
The Authority will verify an individual's Aadhaar number if it's submitted by any requesting organization. This can involve using the person's biometric or demographic information, following specified conditions and payment of specified fees.

Requesting Entity's Responsibilities:
If a requesting organization needs to collect an individual's identity information for verification, they must get the individual's consent (or the consent of a parent/guardian for a child) as per regulations. The identity information should only be used for submission to the Central Identities Data Repository for verification. If verification fails due to various reasons, the organization should provide alternative means of identification as per regulations.

Information to be Provided:
The requesting organization should inform the individual (or the parent/guardian, in the case of a child) about what information may be shared during verification, how the information may be used by the requesting entity, and any alternatives to providing identity information to the entity. The Authority will respond to a verification query with a positive, negative, or other appropriate response, while excluding core biometric information from any shared identity details.

SECTION 11 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
Chapter Iv
Unique Identification Authorityof Inida
11. Establishment of Authority.-
(1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish an Authority to be known as the Unique Identification Authority of India to be responsible for the processes of enrolment and authentication and perform such other functions assigned to it under this Act.
(2) The Authority shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power, subject to the provisions of this Act, to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract, and shall, by the said name, sue or be sued.
(3) The head office of the Authority shall be in New Delhi.
(4) The Authority may, with the prior approval of the Central Government, establish its offices at other places in India.
simplified_text:
Establishment of Unique Identification Authority of India:

1. Creation of Authority: The Central Government will set up an Authority called the Unique Identification Authority of India. This Authority will manage the process of enrolment and authentication, as well as other tasks assigned to it under this Act.

2. Status of the Authority: The Authority will be a separate legal entity with a perpetual existence and a common seal. It has the authority, within the framework of this Act, to own, transfer, and manage both movable and immovable property, as well as to enter into contracts and to engage in legal proceedings using its name.

3. Headquarters: The main office of the Authority will be located in New Delhi.

4. Establishment of Regional Offices: With the prior approval of the Central Government, the Authority can establish offices at other locations in India.

SECTION 14 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
14. Term of office and other conditions of service of Chairperson and Members.-
(1) The Chairperson and the Members appointed under this Act shall hold office for a term of three years from the date on which they assume office and shall be eligible for re-appointment:
Provided that no person shall hold office as the Chairperson or Member after he has attained the age of sixty-five years.
(2) The Chairperson and every Member shall, before entering office, make and subscribe to, an oath of office and of secrecy, in such form and in such manner and before such Authority as may be prescribed.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), the Chairperson or Member may-
(a) relinquish his office, by giving in writing to the Central Government, a notice of not less than thirty days; or
(b) be removed from his office in accordance with the provisions of section 15.
(4) The salaries and allowances payable to, and the other terms and conditions of service of, the Chairperson and allowances or remuneration payable to part-time Members shall be such as may be prescribed.
simplified_text:
Term of Office and Conditions of Service:
- The Chairperson and Members appointed under this Act will hold office for three years from the date they start and can be re-appointed. However, they cannot continue as Chairperson or Member after turning 65 years old.
- Before starting their roles, the Chairperson and each Member must take an oath of office and secrecy as prescribed.
- The Chairperson or Member may resign by giving a written notice of at least thirty days to the Central Government or be removed in accordance with Section 15.
- The salaries, allowances, and other service conditions of the Chairperson, as well as the allowances or remuneration for part-time Members, will be as prescribed.

Removal of Chairperson and Members
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits, and Services) Act, 2016

The Central Government has the authority to remove the Chairperson or a Member if:
- They have been declared bankrupt or insolvent.
- They are no longer capable of performing their duties due to physical or mental incapacity.
- They have been convicted of an offense that, according to the Central Government, involves moral misconduct.
- They have acquired financial or other interests that are likely to negatively impact their role.
- According to the Central Government, they have misused their position in a way that is harmful to the public interest.

The Chairperson or a Member cannot be removed unless they have been given an opportunity to present their case, except in cases involving physical or mental incapacity, acquirement of prejudicial interests, or misuse of their position.

SECTION 16 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
16. Restrictions on Chairperson or Members on employment after cessation of office.-
The Chairperson or a Member on ceasing to hold office for any reason, shall not, without previous approval of the Central Government,-
(a) accept any employment in, or be connected with the management of any organisation, company or any other entity which has been associated with any work done or contracted out by the Authority, whether directly or indirectly, during his tenure as Chairperson or Member, as the case may be, for a period of three years from the date on which he ceases to hold office:
Provided that nothing contained in this clause shall apply to any employment under the Central Government or a State Government or local authority or in any statutory authority or any corporation established by or under any Central, State or provincial Act or a Government Company, as defined in clause (45) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013);
(b) act, for or on behalf of any person or organisation in connection with any specific proceeding or transaction or negotiation or a case to which the Authority is a party and with respect to which the Chairperson or such Member had, before cessation of office, acted for or provided advice to, the Authority;
(c) give advice to any person using information which was obtained in his capacity as the Chairperson or a Member and being unavailable to or not being able to be made available to the public; or
(d) enter, for a period of three years from his last day in office, into a contract of service with, accept an appointment to a board of directors of, or accept an offer of employment with, an entity with which he had direct and significant official dealings during his term of office.
simplified_text:
Restrictions on Employment after Cessation of Office:

After leaving office for any reason, the Chairperson or a Member of the Aadhaar Authority cannot, without prior approval from the Central Government:

a) Take on any job or be involved in managing any organization, company, or entity that had any association with work carried out or contracted during their time as Chairperson or Member for a period of three years.
This does not apply to employment under the Central Government, State Government, local authority, statutory authority, corporation established under central, state, or provincial law, or a government company as defined in the Companies Act, 2013.

b) Act for or on behalf of any person or organization in connection with any specific proceedings, transactions, negotiations, or cases to which the Authority is a party and in which the Chairperson or Member had previously been involved.

c) Provide advice to any person using information obtained during their time as Chairperson or Member which is not available to the public.

d) Enter into a contract of service, accept an appointment to a board of directors, or take up employment with an entity they had direct and significant official dealings with during their term of office, for a period of three years.

Simplified text: Chief Executive Officer

The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits, and Services) Act, 2016

Section 18

(1) The Central Government shall appoint a chief executive officer for the Authority, who should hold a rank not lower than Additional Secretary to the Government of India.

(2) The chief executive officer's responsibilities include:

a) Managing the day-to-day operations of the Authority.

b) Implementing the Authority's work plans and decisions.

c) Developing proposals for the Authority's decisions and work plans.

d) Managing the Authority's budget, including revenue and expenditure statements.

e) Carrying out other functions and powers specified by regulations.

(3) Annually, the chief executive officer must present to the Authority for approval:

a) A comprehensive report on the Authority's activities in the previous year.

b) Work programs.

c) The previous year's financial statements.

d) The budget for the next year.

(4) The chief executive officer has administrative authority over the Authority's officers and employees.

SECTION 19 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
19. Meetings of Authority.-
(1) The Authority shall meet at such times and places and shall observe such rules of procedure in regard to the transaction of business at its meetings, including quorum at such meetings, as may be specified by regulations.
(2) The Chairperson, or, if for any reason, he is unable to attend a meeting of the Authority, the senior most Member shall preside over the meetings of the Authority.
(3) All questions which come up before any meeting of the Authority shall be decided by a majority of votes by the Members present and voting and in the event of anequality of votes, the Chairperson or in his absence the presiding Member shall have a casting vote.
(4) All decisions of the Authority shall be signed by the Chairperson or any other Member or the Member-Secretary authorised by the Authority in this behalf.
(5) If any Member, who is a director of a company and who as such director, has any direct or indirect pecuniary interest in any manner coming up for consideration at a meeting of the Authority, he shall, as soon as possible after relevant circumstances have come to his knowledge, disclose the nature of his interest at such meeting and such disclosure shall be recorded in the proceedings of the Authority, and the Member shall not take part in any deliberation or decision of the Authority with respect to that matter.
simplified_text:
Meetings of Authority:
- The Authority will meet at specified times and places and will follow rules for conducting meetings, including ensuring there are enough members present to make decisions (quorum).
- The Chairperson will preside over meetings. If the Chairperson is unable to attend, the most senior Member will lead the meetings.
- Decisions will be made by a majority vote of the Members present. If there is a tie, the Chairperson or the presiding Member will have the deciding vote.
- All decisions of the Authority must be signed by the Chairperson, another Member, or the Member-Secretary authorized by the Authority.
- If a Member is a director of a company and has a financial interest in a matter being considered, they must disclose their interest at the meeting, and this must be recorded in the Authority's proceedings. The Member cannot take part in the discussion or decision on that matter.

SECTION 22 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
22. Transfer of assets, liabilities of Authority.-
On and from the establishment of the Authority-
(a) all the assets and liabilities of the Unique Identification Authority of India, established vide notification of the Government of India in the Planning Commission number A-43011/02/2009-Admin. I, dated the 28th January, 2009, shall stand transferred to, and vested in, the Authority.
Explanation.- The assets of such Unique Identification Authority of India shall be deemed to include all rights and powers, and all properties, whether movable or immovable, including, in particular, cash balances, deposits and all other interests and rights in, or arising out of, such properties as may be in the possession of such Unique Identification Authority of India and all books of account and other documents relating to the same; and liabilities shall be deemed to include all debts, liabilities and obligations of whatever kind;
(b) without prejudice to the provisions of clause (a), all data and information collected during enrolment, all details of authentication performed, debts, obligations and liabilities incurred, all contracts entered into and all matters and things engaged to be done by, with or for such Unique Identification Authority of India immediately before that day, for or in connection with the purpose of the said Unique Identification Authority of India, shall be deemed to have been incurred, entered into or engaged to be done by, with or for, the Authority;
(c) all sums of money due to the said Unique Identification Authority of India immediately before that day shall be deemed to be due to the Authority; and
(d) all suits and other legal proceedings instituted or which could have been instituted by or against such Unique Identification Authority of India immediately before that day may be continued or may be instituted by or against the Authority.
simplified_text:
Transfer of Assets and Liabilities:

When the Authority is established, the following will happen:
All assets and liabilities of the Unique Identification Authority of India will be transferred to and become the responsibility of the Authority. This includes all rights, powers, properties, cash, and debts, as well as any contracts or legal matters previously handled by the Unique Identification Authority of India. Any money owed to the Unique Identification Authority of India will then be owed to the Authority, and any pending legal proceedings can be carried on by or against the Authority.

Simplified text: Powers and Functions of the Authority under the Aadhaar Act, 2016

1. The Authority's Responsibilities:
The Authority is responsible for creating the policy, procedure, and system for issuing Aadhaar numbers to individuals and authenticating them under this Act.

2. Additional Powers and Functions of the Authority include:
- Specifying the demographic and biometric information needed for enrollment, and the procedures for collection and verification.
- Collecting demographic and biometric information from individuals seeking an Aadhaar number.
- Appointing one or more entities to operate the Central Identities Data Repository.
- Assigning Aadhaar numbers to individuals and authenticating them.
- Maintaining and updating individuals' information in the Central Identities Data Repository.
- Deactivating Aadhaar numbers and related information as specified by regulations.
- Defining the use of Aadhaar numbers for providing subsidies, benefits, services, and other authorized purposes.
- Specifying terms and conditions for appointing Registrars, enrolling agencies, service providers, and revoking their appointments.
- Establishing, operating, and maintaining the Central Identities Data Repository.
- Sharing information of Aadhaar number holders as specified by regulations, subject to the provisions of this Act.
- Conducting inspections, inquiries, and audits relating to the operations under this Act.
- Specifying various processes related to data management, security protocols, and technology safeguards under this Act.
- Defining conditions and procedures for issuing new Aadhaar numbers to existing Aadhaar number holders.
- Levying and collecting fees for services provided under this Act.
- Appointing necessary committees to assist in the discharge of its functions.
- Promoting research and development in biometrics and related areas.
- Evolving and specifying policies and practices for Registrars, enrolling agencies, and other service providers.
- Setting up facilitation centers and grievance redressal mechanisms.
- Exercising any other powers and functions as prescribed.

3. Authority's Collaborations:
The Authority may enter into agreements with the government or other agencies to carry out its functions. It may also appoint Registrars and engage agencies as necessary through notification.

4. Engagement of Consultants and Advisors:
The Authority may engage consultants, advisors, and other necessary personnel to efficiently carry out its functions as specified by contract.

SECTION 26 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
26. Accounts and audit.-
(1) The Authority shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare an annual statement of accounts in such form as may be prescribed by the Central Government in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
(2) The accounts of the Authority shall be audited annually by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India at such intervals as may be specified by him and any expenditure incurred in connection with such audit shall be payable by the Authority to the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
(3) The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and any person appointed by him in connection with the audit the accounts of the Authority under this Act shall have the same rights and privileges and authority in connection with such audit as the Comptroller and Auditor-General generally has in connection with the audit of Government accounts, and in particular, shall have the right to demand production of books, accounts, connected vouchers and other documents and papers, and to inspect any of the offices of the Authority.
(4) The accounts of the Authority, as certified by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India or any other person appointed by him in this behalf, together with the audit report thereon shall be forwarded annually to the Central Government by the Authority and the Central Government shall cause the audit report to be laid, as soon as may be after it is received, before each House of Parliament.
simplified_text:
Simplified text: 

Accounts and Audit of Aadhaar Authority:

The Aadhaar Authority is required to maintain accurate accounts and relevant records. It must prepare an annual financial statement in a format prescribed by the Central Government in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

The Authority's accounts will be audited annually by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India at specified intervals. The Authority is responsible for the expenses related to this audit.

The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, along with any appointees, has the same rights and authority to audit the Authority's accounts as they have when auditing government accounts. This includes the right to request production of documents and inspect the Authority's offices.

The certified accounts of the Authority, accompanied by the audit report, must be submitted annually to the Central Government. Upon receipt, the Central Government must promptly present the audit report to each House of Parliament.

SECTION 27 of Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
27. Returns and annual report, etc.-
(1) The Authority shall furnish to the Central Government at such time and in such form and manner as may be prescribed or as the Central Government may direct, such returns and statements and particulars in regard to any matter under the jurisdiction of the Authority, as the Central Government may from time to time require.
(2) The Authority shall prepare, once in every year, and in such form and manner and at such time as may be prescribed, an annual report giving-
(a) a description of all the activities of the Authority for the previous years;
(b) the annual accounts for the previous year; and
(c) the programmes of work for coming year.
(3) A copy of the report received under sub-section (2) shall be laid by the Central Government, as soon as may be after it is received, before each House of Parliament.

Simplified text: Offences by Companies under Actuaries Act, 2006

1. If a company commits an offence under this Act, both the company and every person in charge of its business at the time of the offence are considered guilty and can be punished. However, a person can avoid punishment if they can prove that they were not aware of the offence or had taken all necessary steps to prevent it.

2. In addition, if it is proven that an offence was committed with the knowledge or negligence of any director, manager, secretary, or officer of the company, they will also be held accountable for the offence and can be punished accordingly.

Explanation:
- "Company" includes any body corporate, firm, or association of individuals.
- In a firm, a "director" refers to a partner in the firm.

The Central Government will set up an Administrative Tribunal, known as the Central Administrative Tribunal, to handle specific legal matters as outlined in this Act.
At the request of a State Government, the Central Government can establish a State-specific Administrative Tribunal for that state to address similar legal matters.
Multiple states can agree to have a single Administrative Tribunal to serve them all. Once the agreement is approved by the Central Government and relevant states, a Joint Administrative Tribunal will be created to oversee legal matters specified in this Act for all participating states.

Simplified text: Qualifications for Administrative Tribunal Members:

Chairman Eligibility:
To be appointed as the Chairman, a person must meet one of the following criteria:
- Previous or current Judge of a High Court.
- Previous Vice-Chairman for at least two years.

Vice-Chairman Eligibility:
To be appointed as the Vice-Chairman, a person must meet one of the following criteria:
- Previous or current Judge of a High Court.
- Previous Secretary to the Government of India or equivalent position for at least two years with appropriate pay scale.
- Previous Additional Secretary to the Government of India or equivalent position for at least five years with appropriate pay scale.
- Judicial Member or Administrative Member for at least three years.

Judicial Member Eligibility:
To be appointed as a Judicial Member, a person must meet one of the following criteria:
- Previous or current Judge of a High Court.
- Member of the Indian Legal Service with Grade I experience for at least three years.

Administrative Member Eligibility:
To be appointed as an Administrative Member, a person must have one of the following:
- Previous Additional Secretary to the Government of India or equivalent position for at least two years with appropriate pay scale.
- Previous Joint Secretary to the Government of India or equivalent position for at least three years with appropriate pay scale, along with sufficient administrative experience.

Appointment:
The President appoints the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and all other Members of the Administrative Tribunal (including state and joint tribunals), in consultation with relevant authorities as specified. The Chief Justice of India must also be consulted before making any such appointments.

Simplified text: Jurisdiction and Powers of State Administrative Tribunals
The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Jurisdiction, Powers, and Authority of State Administrative Tribunals:
The Administrative Tribunals in each State will have the authority to handle all legal matters and issues previously dealt with by other courts, excluding the Supreme Court, for the following:

Recruitment: Matters related to the recruitment of civil service positions or civil posts within the State.
Service Matters: Concerns regarding individuals employed in civil services or civil posts within the State, involving the State's affairs or any related authority, corporation, or society under State control or ownership.
State Government Notification:
The State Government can extend the application of specific provisions to various local authorities, corporations, or societies under its control or ownership through an official notification.
Transition Period:
To facilitate a smooth transition in accordance with the Act's provisions, the State Government can set different effective dates for different classes or categories of authorities, corporations, or societies.
Additional Powers of Administrative Tribunals:
Administrative Tribunals will also have the power to manage legal matters related to recruitment or service within local authorities, corporations, or societies to which the Act's provisions apply.
Limitations:
The authority of State Administrative Tribunals does not cover matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal.

SECTION 19 of Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
19. Applications to Tribunals. -
(1) Subject to the other provisions of this

Act, a person aggrieved by any order pertaining to any matter within the

jurisdiction of a Tribunal may make an application to the Tribunal for the

redressal of his grievance. 
Explanation :
(a) by the Government or a local or other

authority within the territory of India or under the control of the Government

of India or by any corporation or society owned or controlled by the

Government; or 
(b) by an officer, committee or other body or

agency of the Government or a local or other authority or corporation or

society referred to in clause (a). 
(2) Every application under sub-section (1)

shall be in such form and be accompanied by such documents or other evidence

and by such fee (if any, not exceeding one hundred rupees) in respect of the

filing of such application and by such other fees for the service or execution

of processes, as may be prescribed by the Central Government. 
(3) On receipt of an application under

sub-section (1), the Tribunal shall, if satisfied after such inquiry as it may

deem necessary, that the application is a fit case for adjudication or trial by

it, admit such application; but where the Tribunal is not so satisfied, it may

summarily reject the application after recording its reasons. 
(4) Where an application has been admitted by

a Tribunal under sub-section (3), every proceeding under the relevant service

rules as to redressal of grievances in relation to the subject-matter of such

application pending immediately before such admission shall abate and save as

otherwise direct by the Tribunal, no appeal or representation in relation to

such matter shall thereafter be entertained under such rules. 
Comments: It is settled law that the Tribunal

has only power of judicial review of the administrative action of the appellant

on complaints relating to service conditions of employees. It is the exclusive

domain of the disciplinary authority to consider the evidence on record and to

record findings whether the charge has been proved or not. It is equally

settled law that technical rules of evidence has no application for the

disciplinary proceedings and the authority is to consider the material on

record. In judicial review, it is settled law that the Court or the Tribunal

has no power to trench on the jurisdiction to appreciate the evidence and to

arrive at its own conclusion. State of T.N. v. S. Subramaniam, AIR 1996

SUPREME COURT 1232
simplified_text:
Simplified text: Applications to Tribunals:

If someone is upset by a decision related to something a Tribunal is in charge of, they can file a complaint with the Tribunal to try and fix the problem.

Clarification:
This applies to decisions made by:
- The Government or any local or other authority in India under Government control.
- Any organization owned or controlled by the Government.
- An official, committee, or organization linked to the Government or a local or other authority or the organizations mentioned above.

Filing a Complaint:
When making a complaint to the Tribunal:
- Use the required form.
- Submit any necessary documents or evidence.
- Pay a fee (up to one hundred rupees) for filing the complaint and any other fees if needed for processing.

Review by the Tribunal:
Once a complaint is submitted, the Tribunal will review it. If the Tribunal believes the complaint is suitable for further review or trial, it will accept it. Otherwise, it may reject the complaint after explaining why.

Effects of Acceptance:
If the Tribunal accepts a complaint, any ongoing processes within the service rules related to the complaint will stop. Unless the Tribunal says otherwise, no appeals or representations on the matter will be accepted under those rules.

Note: The Tribunal has the authority to review administrative actions based on complaints about employee service conditions. The responsibility of analyzing evidence and determining if charges are proven lies with the disciplinary authority. Technical evidence rules do not apply in disciplinary proceedings; the authority must base its decisions on the available evidence. During a judicial review, the Court or Tribunal cannot interfere with the authority's fact-finding role. (State of T.N. v. S. Subramaniam, AIR 1996 SUPREME COURT 1232)

  (3) For the purposes of sub-sections (1) and

simplified_text:
Simplified text: Exhaustion of Remedies Before Applying to Tribunal

A Tribunal will usually not consider an application unless it is sure that the applicant has already tried all the available options for resolving the issue through the service rules.

To be considered to have exhausted all available remedies under the service rules for resolving grievances:
- A person is considered to have done so if the government or any competent authority has issued a final order denying any appeal or representation made by the person regarding the grievance.
- If no final order has been issued within six months from the date of the appeal or representation, it is also considered that all remedies have been exhausted.

Note that submitting a memorial to the President, Governor, or any other official will not be considered as exhausting remedies unless the applicant chooses to do so.

Simplified text: Time Limits for Filing Applications: An application cannot be accepted by a Tribunal in the following situations:

A. For a case where a final order has been issued regarding the issue, the application must be submitted within one year from the date the order was issued.
B. For a case where an appeal has been made, but no final order has been issued after six months, the application must be submitted within one year after the six-month period expires.

Exceptions to Time Limits:
A. If the issue arose due to an order made within three years before the Tribunal gained jurisdiction, and no action had been taken in a High Court, the application can be considered if filed within the specified time limits or within six months of the Tribunal gaining jurisdiction, whichever is later.
B. An application may be accepted after the specified time limits if the applicant can prove to the Tribunal that there was a valid reason for the delay.

(2) A tribunal shall decide every application

be decided on a perusal of documents and written representations and after hearing

such oral arguments as may be advanced. 
(3) A Tribunal shall have, for the purposes of

discharging its functions under this Act, the same powers as are vested in a

civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), while trying a

suit, in respect of the following matters, namely : 
(a) Summoning and

enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; 
 (b) requiring the

discovery and production of documents; 
 (c) receiving evidence

on affidavits; 
(d) subject to the provisions

of section 123 and 124 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (1 of 1872),

requisitioning any public record or document or copy of such record or document

from any office; 
 (e) issuing

commissions for the examination of witnesses or, documents; 
 (f) reviewing its

decisions; 
 (g) dismissing a

(h) setting aside any

Simplified text: Procedure and Powers of Tribunals under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985

1. Operating Procedure:
  - The Tribunal is not required to follow the rules of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908. Instead, it must adhere to the principles of natural justice.
  - The Tribunal has the authority to set its own procedure, including choosing when and where to hold inquiries and deciding whether they will be public or private.

2. Deciding Applications:
  - The Tribunal must process applications promptly, mainly based on written documents and oral arguments when necessary.

3. Powers of the Tribunal:
  - The Tribunal has the same powers as a civil court under the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, for various purposes:
     a. Summoning individuals and taking their oath.
     b. Requesting documents to be produced.
     c. Accepting evidence through affidavits.
     d. Obtaining public records or copies from offices.
     e. Issuing commissions for witness examinations or document reviews.
     f. Reviewing its decisions.
     g. Dismissing or deciding applications if there is a default or if one party doesn't participate.
     h. Overturning orders made due to defaults or ex parte decisions.
     i. Handling other matters specified by the Central Government.

Simplified text: Conditions for Interim Orders: 

No interim orders (temporary orders like injunctions or stays) can be issued without following these steps:
- Provide copies of the application and supporting documents to the other party.
- Give the other party a chance to be heard.

A tribunal can skip these steps and issue an interim order if it believes that not doing so might cause irreparable harm to the applicant. However, the order will only last for 14 days unless the requirements are met before that deadline and the tribunal decides to extend it.

When a Tribunal is established, certain cases from courts or other authorities will be moved to the Tribunal if the cause of action would fall under the Tribunal's jurisdiction if it had arisen after the Tribunal was set up. Explanation:

When a Joint Administrative Tribunal is set up for multiple states, cases from existing State Tribunals will be transferred to the Joint Tribunal.

- Admiralty Proceeding: Legal actions conducted before a High Court with admiralty jurisdiction.
- Arrest: Restraining or seizing a vessel by court order to secure a maritime claim, including enforcing a judgment.
- Goods: Any type of property, including live animals, containers, pallets, or other transport-related items, on or under a vessel's deck.
- High Court: Refers to specific High Courts or any other designated by the Central Government for admiralty proceedings.
- Maritime Claim: Claims specified in section 4 of the Act.
- Maritime Lien: A claim against the vessel owner, charterer, manager, or operator as described in the Act.
- Notification: An announcement published in the Official Gazette.
- Port: Defined as in the Indian Ports Act, 1908.
- Prescribed: Terms established by Central Government rules under this Act.
- Territorial Waters: Defined as in the Territorial Waters Act, 1976.
- Vessel: Includes various watercraft used or built for navigation, even if not powered, and covers specific types of floating vessels and structures.

Simplified text: Maritime Claims
Court Authority: The High Court has the power to resolve disputes related to maritime claims concerning a vessel. These disputes may involve various issues including:
Ownership Disputes: Disagreements over vessel ownership or shares in a vessel.
Co-ownership Disputes: Disputes between co-owners of a vessel regarding its use or earnings.
Mortgage Claims: Claims related to mortgages or charges on a vessel.
Damage Claims: Claims for loss or damage caused by a vessel's operation.
Injury Claims: Claims for personal injury or loss of life linked to a vessel's operation.
Cargo Disputes: Disputes concerning goods carried on a vessel.
Agreements: Claims arising from agreements for goods or passenger transport or vessel use.
Salvage and Services: Claims for salvage services, towage, pilotage, and related services.
Supplies and Dues: Claims for supplies, services, dues, and charges related to vessel operations.

Vessel Preservation: Costs related to raising, removal, or preservation of a vessel.
Maritime Liens: Claims related to maritime liens on vessels.
Court Actions: The High Court has the authority to settle accounts, order vessel sales, and resolve title disputes. Vessels or proceeds from sales may be held as security during legal proceedings.

5. Arrest of vessel in rem.
(1) The High Court may order arrest of any vessel which is within its jurisdiction for the purpose of providing security against a maritime claim which is the subject of an admiralty proceeding, where the court has reason to believe that-

(c) the claim is based on a mortgage or a charge of the similar nature on the vessel; or

SECTION 7 of Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017
7. Restrictions on actions in personam in certain cases.
(1) Where any maritime claim arising in respect of a damage or loss of life or personal injury arising out of any-
(i) collision between vessels,
(ii) the carrying out of or omission to carry out, a manoeuvre in the case of one or more vessels,
(iii) non-compliance, on the part of one or more vessels, with the collision regulations made in pursuance of section 285 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 (44 of 1958), the High Court shall not entertain any action under this section against any defendant unless-
(a) the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises in India; or
(b) the defendant, at the time of commencement of the action by the High Court, actually and voluntarily resides or carries on business or personally works for gain in India:
Provided that an action may be entertained in a case, where there are more defendants than one and where one of the defendants who does not actually and voluntarily reside or carry on business or personally work for gain in India is made a party to such action either with the leave of the court, or each of the defendants acquiesces in such action.
(2) The High Court shall not entertain any action in personam to enforce a claim to which this section applies until any proceedings previously brought by the plaintiff in any court outside India against the same defendant in respect of the same incident or series of incidents have been discontinued or have otherwise come to an end.
(3) The provisions of sub-section (2) shall apply to counter-claims as they apply to actions except counter-claims in proceedings arising out of the same incident or series of incidents.
(4) A reference to the plaintiff and the defendant for the purpose of sub-section (3) shall be construed as reference to the plaintiff in the counter-claim and the defendant in the counter-claim respectively.
(5) The provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3) shall not apply to any action or counter-claim if the defendant submits or agrees to submit to the jurisdiction of the High Court.
(6) Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), the High Court shall have jurisdiction to entertain an action in personam to enforce a claim to which this section applies whenever any of the conditions specified, in clauses (a)and (b) of sub-section (1) is satisfied and any law for the time being in force relating to the service of process outside the jurisdiction shall apply.

Simplified text: Restrictions on Legal Actions in Maritime Cases

When it comes to maritime claims involving damage, loss of life, or personal injury due to:
- Vessel collisions,
- Maneuvers (or a failure to maneuver) by one or more vessels, 
- Non-compliance with collision regulations specified in the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958,

The High Court in India can only hear a case against a defendant if:
a) The incident occurred in India, or
b) The defendant resides, conducts business, or works in India at the time the legal action is initiated.

Exceptions are made if there are multiple defendants, and at least one defendant is not based in India but agrees to the court's jurisdiction.

Before initiating a legal action in India, the plaintiff must conclude any legal proceedings against the same defendant in another country regarding the same incident.

Counter-claims are subject to the same rules, except when they involve the same incident or incidents.

Defendants can bypass these rules by agreeing to the court's jurisdiction.

The High Court has the authority to hear such cases if the conditions mentioned above are met, and international service of process laws are followed.

Simplified text: Inter se Priority of Maritime Liens:
Priority Order: All maritime liens are prioritized in the following order:
Wages and other amounts owed to the vessel's crew, including repatriation costs and social insurance contributions.
Loss of life or personal injury directly related to the vessel's operation.
Salvage service rewards and special compensations.
Port, canal, waterway, pilotage, and other statutory dues.
Tort claims for damages caused by the vessel's operation (excluding cargo and containers).
Continuation and Expiry:
Maritime liens remain on the vessel even if ownership, registration, or flag changes, but expire after one year unless the vessel is arrested and forced to be sold by the High Court. For crew-related claims, the period is two years from when the payment is due.
Commencement:
For crew-related liens, upon discharge from the vessel; for other liens, when the claim arises, without any interruptions except during vessel arrest or seizure.
Exceptions:
No maritime lien can secure claims arising from oil or hazardous substance transportation damages compensated by existing laws, or from radioactive substances.

SECTION 11 of Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017
11. Protection of owner, demise charterer, manager or operator or crew of vessel arrested.
(1) The High Court may, as a condition of arrest of a vessel, or for permitting an arrest already effected to be maintained, impose upon the claimant who seeks to arrest or who has procured the arrest of the vessel, an obligation to provide an unconditional undertaking to pay such sums of money as damages or such security of a kind for an amount and upon such terms as may be determined by the High Court, for any loss or damage which may be incurred by the defendant as a result of the arrest, and for which the claimant may be found liable, including but not restricted to the following, namely:-
(a) the arrest having been wrongful or unjustified; or
(b) excessive security having been demanded and provided.
(2) Where pursuant to sub-section (1), the person providing the security may at any time, apply to the High Court to have the security reduced, modified or cancelled for sufficient reasons as may be stated in the application.
(3) If the owner or demise charterer abandons the vessel after its arrest, the High Court shall cause the vessel to be auctioned and the proceeds appropriated and dealt with in such manner as the court may deem fit within a period of forty-five days from the date of arrest or abandonment:
Provided that the High Court shall, for reasons to be recorded in writing, extend the period of auction of the vessel for a further period of thirty days.

Adjusting Security: The person providing the security can ask the High Court to change or cancel it for valid reasons.

Simplified text: State Bar Councils and Advocates Roll Maintenance

Creating and Updating List: Every State Bar Council must establish and keep a record of advocates. This list should include:

1. Those who were registered as advocates in any High Court under the Indian Bar Councils Act, 1926, before a specified day. This includes Indian citizens who were enrolled as advocates under this Act in any area within India as defined before August 15, 1947, and have expressed an intention to practice within the Council's jurisdiction following the proper procedure.
2. All other individuals admitted as advocates by the State Bar Council after the specified day.

Roll Structure: The advocate list maintained by each State Bar Council shall contain two sections - one for senior advocates and the other for remaining advocates.

Order of Seniority: The order of seniority for advocates on each list will be determined as follows: 
a. For advocates under the Indian Bar Council Act, 1926, seniority is based on their enrollment date.
b. For individuals who were senior advocates of the Supreme Court before the specified day, seniority in the first part of the State list follows principles set by the Bar Council of India.
c. There are no determinants for seniority under clause c.
d. Those enrolled as senior advocates or advocates after the appointed day have their seniority determined by their enrollment or admission date.
e. Seniority of an attorney later enrolled as an advocate follows their attorney enrollment date, as per the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1980.

Single Enrollment: No individual can be registered as an advocate with more than one State Bar Council.

The Advocates Act, 1961, outlines the order of precedence for legal representatives as follows:
The Attorney General of India holds the highest precedence over all other advocates.

Admission as an Advocate on a State Roll:

To be admitted as an advocate on a State roll, a person must meet certain conditions:

1. Citizenship: The individual must be a citizen of India. However, a citizen of another country may also be admitted if Indian citizens are allowed to practice law in that country.
2. Age: The person must be at least twenty-one years old.
3. Legal Qualifications:
   - Obtain a law degree from an Indian university before March 12, 1967, or before August 15, 1947, from a university in the pre-independence Indian territories defined by the Government of India Act, 1935.
   - Complete a three-year law course from a recognized Indian university after March 12, 1967, or a two-year course from the academic year 1967-98 onwards.
   - Be a barrister or possess a foreign law qualification recognized by the Bar Council of India.
   - In other cases, obtain a law degree from a foreign university recognized by the Bar Council of India.
4. Other Conditions: Fulfill any additional requirements set by the State Bar Council.
5. Fees: Pay the prescribed stamp duty and enrollment fee to the State Bar Council and the Bar Council of India. Reduced fees apply for members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes upon providing the necessary certification.

Special Considerations:
- A law graduate who is a vakil or a pleader may be admitted within two years of the specified date if they meet specific conditions.
- Certain individuals with legal experience or entitlements from specific regions or conditions may also be admitted if they fulfill the necessary requirements.

Simplified text: Definitions:
Advocate: A lawyer whose name is listed in the State Bar Council's register under the Advocates Act, 1961, and is a member of a State Bar Association or State Advocates' Association.
Appropriate Government:
In the case of advocates in a State Bar Council, it's the State Government.
For advocates in a Union territory Bar Council, it's the Central Government.
Cessation of Practice: Removing an advocate's name from the State Bar Council register under the Advocates Act, 1961.
Chairperson: The head of the Trustee Committee specified in section 4.
Chartered Accountant: A professional defined in the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, with a practice certificate.
Dependents: Spouse, parents, or minor children of a Fund member.
Fund: The Advocates' Welfare Fund established under section 3.
Insurer: Defined as per the Insurance Act, 1938.
Member of the Fund: An advocate entitled to Fund benefits and maintaining membership under this Act.
Notification: An official announcement released by the relevant Government in the Official Gazette.
Prescribed: Guidelines set in rules under this Act.
Schedule: A table attached to this Act.
Scheduled Bank: Defined in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Stamp: A special Fund stamp issued under section 26.
State: Refers to a state as per the Constitution, including Union territories.
State Advocates' Association: Recognized advocates' association in a State under section 16.
State Bar Association: Advocates' association acknowledged by the State Bar Council under section 16.
State Bar Council: Bar Council as per the Advocates Act, 1961.
Suspension of Practice: Voluntary or disciplinary suspension of an advocate by a State Bar Council.
Trustee Committee: The committee overseeing the Advocates' Welfare Fund.
Vakalatnama: A document authorizing an advocate to represent a client before a court or authority.
Unspecified Terms: Terms not defined in this Act but in the Advocates Act, 1961 carry the definitions from that Act.

Simplified text: Disqualifications and Removal from Office:
The Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 2001
Section 5

The government can remove the chairperson or any member of the Trustee Committee if they:

Have been declared bankrupt.
Are unable to perform their duties due to physical or mental incapacity.
Have been found guilty of a serious crime that the government considers morally wrong.

Simplified text: Membership in Advocates' Welfare Fund

1. Any advocate practicing in a court, tribunal, or other authority in a State who is a member of a State Bar Association or a State Advocates' Association must apply to the Trustee Committee within six months of this Act taking effect to become a member of the Fund.
2. Any person admitted as an advocate on a State Bar Council's roll after this Act's commencement, practicing in a State's court, tribunal, or other authority, and a member of a State Bar Association or State Advocates' Association, must apply to the Trustee Committee within six months of enrollment as an advocate to become a Fund member.
3. The Trustee Committee will review the applications, may conduct an inquiry, and either admit or reject applicants. Rejection requires written reasons after giving applicants a chance to be heard.
4. Applicants must pay a two hundred rupees application fee to the Trustee Committee.
5. Fund members must pay a fifty rupees annual subscription by March 31st each year. Newly admitted members pay their first subscription within three months of joining. Senior advocates pay one thousand rupees annually.
6. Failure to pay the annual subscription by March 31st results in potential removal from Fund membership. 
7. Removal from Fund membership can be reversed within six months by paying arrears and a ten rupees re-admission fee.
8. Upon joining the Fund, members must nominate dependents to receive any entitlements in case of the member's death.
9. If multiple nominees are named, the share for each must be specified. 
10. Members can cancel a nomination at any time by notifying the Trustee Committee in writing.
11. Cancelling a nomination requires making a new one with a five rupees registration fee.
12. If a member's name is removed from the State roll or practice is voluntarily suspended, they must inform the Trustee Committee within fifteen days. Failing to do so may lead to a reduction in entitlements under prescribed rules.

SECTION 10 of African Development Fund Act, 1982
Article 43
Legal Process
1. The Fund shall enjoy immunity from every form of legal process, except in cases arising out of or in connection with the exercise of its power to receive loans in accordance with Article 8, in which case actions may be brought against the Fund in a court of competent jurisdiction in the territory of a country in which the Fund has its office, or has appointed an agent for the purpose of accepting service or notice of process, or has otherwise agreed to be sued.
2. Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 1, no action shall be brought against the Fund by any participant, or by any agency or instrumentality of a participant, or by any entity or person directly or indirectly acting for or deriving claims from a participant or from any agency or instrumentality of a participant. Participants shall have recourse to such special procedures for the settlement of disputes between the Fund and its participants as may be prescribed in this Agreement, in the bye-laws and regulations of the Fund, or in contracts entered into with the Fund.
3. The Fund shall also make provision for appropriate modes of settlement of disputes in cases which do not come within the provisions of paragraph 2 and of Articles 52 and 53 and which are subject to the immunity of the Fund by virtue of paragraph 1 of this Article.
4. Where by virtue of any of the provisions of this Agreement the Fund does not enjoy immunity from legal process, the Fund, and its property and assets wherever located and by whomsoever held, shall nevertheless be immune from all forms of seizure, attachment or execution before the delivery of final judgment against the Fund.

Simplified text:
Legal Process: African Development Fund Act, 1982

1. Immunity from Legal Process: The Fund is protected from legal actions in most cases. However, if a case is related to its power to receive loans, legal actions can be taken against the Fund in a court where it operates, has appointed an agent, or agreed to be sued.

2. Exceptions to Immunity: Participants, agencies, or entities linked to participants cannot sue the Fund. Disputes between the Fund and participants must follow specific procedures outlined in agreements, bye-laws, regulations, or contracts.

3. Dispute Settlement: The Fund must provide methods to resolve disputes not covered in paragraph 2 and Articles 52 and 53 while maintaining its immunity from legal actions.

4. Protection of Assets: Even when the Fund is not immune from legal process, its assets cannot be seized, attached, or executed until a final judgment is delivered.

Simplified text: Duties on Exported Agricultural and Processed Food Products

To support the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act of 1985, a customs duty called a "cess" is imposed on products listed in the schedule that are being exported. The Central Government, through an official notification, sets the rate of this duty, which cannot exceed three percent of the value of the products.

This duty is in addition to any other taxes or duties that may apply to these products under different laws. The Customs Act of 1962 and its related rules and regulations, including those on refunds and duty exemptions, apply to the collection of this customs duty to the extent they are relevant.

Simplified text: Definitions:
Authority: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority established under section 4 is called the "Authority."
Chairman: The head of the Authority is referred to as the "Chairman."
Export: Moving products out of India by land, sea, or air.
Exporter: Someone registered as an exporter of scheduled products under section 12.
Member: A person who is part of the Authority, including the Chairman.
Prescribed: Defined by rules made under this Act.
Processing: Involves preserving scheduled or special products through methods like canning, freezing, drying, salting, smoking, peeling, or filleting, as specified by the Authority.
Regulations: Rules created under this Act.
Scheduled product: Any agricultural or processed food products listed in the First Schedule.
Special product: Any agricultural or processed food products listed in the Second Schedule.

Legal text: Monitoring and Regulation
The Authority has a duty to monitor and regulate the activities related to exporting agricultural and processed food products. This includes overseeing the production and transportation of these goods, as well as any supporting activities. The Authority is authorized to gather information to carry out its monitoring responsibilities effectively. Additionally, the Authority must provide requested information to the Secretary of State or the Competition and Markets Authority when it pertains to its regulatory functions under this Act.

Simplified text: Oversight and Information Gathering
The Authority is responsible for supervising and controlling the export of agricultural and processed food products. This involves monitoring production, transportation, and related activities. The Authority can collect data to fulfill its monitoring role efficiently. Furthermore, it must share relevant information with the Secretary of State or the Competition and Markets Authority as required for its regulatory duties under this Act.

Simplified text: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) Establishment:

1. Establishment and Structure:
The Authority called the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority is set up by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette. It is a corporate body with continuous existence, a common seal, and the ability to own property, make contracts, and take legal action.

2. Office Location:
The main office of the Authority is in Delhi, and it can open additional offices or agencies in India or internationally with the Central Government's approval.

3. Members:
The Authority consists of:
- Chairman appointed by the Central Government
- Agricultural Marketing Adviser to the Government of India
- Member representing the Planning Commission
- Members from Parliament
- Members representing various government ministries
- Members representing States and Union territories
- Members representing specific organizations related to agriculture and exports
- Members from different industries such as fruits and vegetables, meat, poultry, dairy, and more
- Members appointed from specialists in agriculture, economics, and marketing

4. Term and Functions:
The rules for the members' term of office, vacancies, and conduct are set by regulations. Only officers from the Central Government can attend meetings without voting rights. The Authority's actions are valid even if there are vacancies in its structure, irregularities in appointments, or procedural shortcomings.

5. Meetings:
The Authority will meet as needed and follow specific meeting procedures outlined in regulations.

SECTION 8 of Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985
8. Special provision for transfer of employees to the Authority.-
(1) On the establishment of the Authority, it shall be lawful for the Central Government to transfer to the Authority, by order, and with effect from such date or dates as may be specified in the order, any officer or other employee holding office as such in the Processed Foods Export Promotion Council (hereafter in this section referred to as the Council) immediately before the date on which the Authority is established:
Provided that the scale of pay of the post in the Authority to which such officer or other employee is transferred shall not be lower than the scale of pay of the post he was holding immediately before such transfer and the other terms and conditions of service (including pension, leave, provident fund and medical benefits) of the post to which he is transferred shall not be less favourable than the terms and conditions of service in relation to the post held by him immediately before such transfer.
(2) An order under sub-section (1) may be made so as to have retrospective effect from a date not earlier than the date of the commencement of this Act.
(3) Before any order is issued under sub-section (1), all officers and employees of the Council shall be given an option to express, in such form as may be prescribed, and within such time as may be specified in that behalf by the Central Government, their willingness or otherwise to become employees of the Authority and such option once exercised shall be final:
Provided that no order under sub-section (1) shall be made in relation to any officer or other employees of the Council who has intimated his intention of not becoming an employee of the Authority within the time specified in that behalf:
Provided further that such of the officers and employees of the Council who do not express, within the time specified in that behalf, their intention of becoming the employees of the Authority, shall be dealt with in the same manner and in accordance with the same laws and standing orders as would have applied immediately before the commencement of this Act to the employees of the Council in the event of the reduction of the strength of the officers and employees of the Council.
(4) An officer or other employee transferred by an order made under sub-section (1) shall, on and from the date of transfer, cease to be an employee of the Council and become an officer or other employee of the Authority with such designation as the Authority may determine and shall, subject to the provisions of the proviso to sub-section (1), be governed by the regulations made by the Authority under this Act in respect of remuneration and other conditions of service (including pension, leave, provident fund and medical benefits) and shall continue to be an officer or other employee of the Authority unless and until his employment is duly terminated by the Authority:
Provided that till such time as the regulations referred to above governing the conditions of service of its officers or other employees are framed by the Authority, the relevant laws and standing orders applicable to the officers and employees of the Council shall continue to be applicable to them.
(5) If a question arises whether the terms and conditions of service prescribed in the regulations framed by the Authority in respect of any matter, including remuneration, pension, leave, provident fund and medical benefits, are less favourable than those attached to the post held by an officer or other employee immediately before his transfer to the Authority, the decision of the Central Government in the matter shall be final.
